name: Stone
lede: Stone is a grayish yellow that Maerz and Paul trace back to 1663, far older than most of ColorHub's landscape names, and one of the most common colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A name four centuries old
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates Stone to 1663, long before most other names in this library; the 1955 ISCC-NBS system classes the color as a pale orange yellow, block 73 [1]. The xkcd color survey of 2010 independently landed on nearly the same swatch, under its own crowd-sourced name [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[yellowish-grey]] and [[eucalyptus]], at 
[[sage]], [[ash]], [[khaki]] and [[taupe]] all turn up far more often than chance in paintings that also carry this color [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to Stone in 3,575 of 23,781 paintings, about 15 percent, roughly one painting in seven, as photographed [2]. It plays a highlight in 83 percent of its appearances, the light note in a composition rather than the shadow [2]. Its presence barely shifts century by century, staying within about 20 percent of the archive's overall rate from the 1100s to the 1900s, an unusually flat curve for a color this common [2].

The earliest dated match is a work cataloged to around 300 BCE, *The Kill*, twenty centuries before Maerz and Paul's date, which only shows a similar screen color was photographed there, not that the name or a matching material existed that early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
